subject: tech
title: When It Doesn't Work
about: What to do when a device stops working, in order: stay calm, say what is wrong in the right words (frozen, crashed, no Wi-Fi, won't charge), check the easy things (volume, headphones, cable, battery), close the app and open it again, restart with a grown-up, then ask for help, plus the spinning wheel that means wait, trying one fix at a time, a warm tablet that needs a rest, a crash that is not your fault, and never shaking or hitting it. NC K2-CS-04 (describe basic hardware and software problems with accurate terminology) and K2-CS-02 (hardware parts). Read it together; it goes deeper than the three fix-it cards in Taking Care of Devices.
tip: Next time something freezes, let him lead: stay calm, say the problem in words, check the easy things, close and reopen, then come get you.

cards.q: The game stops working. What is the very first thing to do?
cards.note: Machines break sometimes, so take a breath. A calm head finds the fix faster.

cards.q: Which words help a grown-up fix the problem the fastest?
cards.note: Use the real words: frozen, no sound, no Wi-Fi, won't charge. Then a grown-up knows where to look.

cards.q: You tap and tap but the screen does not change. What is the word for this?
cards.note: Frozen means the app does not answer your taps. Wait a little, then close it.

cards.q: A little wheel spins round and round on the screen. What should you do?
cards.note: The spinning wheel means the tablet is busy working. Tapping more only gives it more to do, so wait.

cards.q: Before you ask for help, which easy things do you check?
cards.note: Easy things first: is the volume up, is the charger plugged in, is the battery empty? Look, but let a grown-up touch the plug.

cards.q: The volume is up but there is still no sound. What might be plugged in?
cards.note: Headphones plugged in send all the sound to the headphones. Unplug them and the speaker works again.

cards.q: The Wi-Fi picture at the top of the screen has no bars. What does that mean?
cards.note: The Wi-Fi picture shows little curved bars, and no bars means no Wi-Fi. A grown-up can turn it back on.

cards.q: The charger is plugged in but the battery is not filling up. What might be loose?
cards.note: A charger cable can wiggle loose at either end. A grown-up pushes both ends in, because only grown-ups touch the outlet.

cards.q: You closed the frozen app. What do you try next?
cards.note: Close it, wait a moment, open it again. That fixes many stuck apps.

cards.q: The screen is so dim you can hardly see it. What do you turn up?
cards.note: Brightness is how much the screen glows, and you can slide it up a little. Bright sun also makes a screen look dim, so move into the shade.

cards.q: Turning it off and on again fixes many problems. Why does it work?
cards.note: Everything stops and starts over clean, like a good night of sleep. The stuck part gets unstuck.

cards.q: The tablet is stuck. Does shaking or hitting it help?
cards.note: Shaking and hitting can break the tablet for good. Gentle hands fix things.

cards.q: You tried the easy things and it still does not work. What now?
cards.note: Asking for help is a smart step, not giving up. Tell the grown-up what you already tried.

cards.q: An app closes all by itself in the middle of a game. What do grown-ups call that?
cards.note: A crash is when an app stops and closes on its own. Open it again, and if it keeps crashing, tell a grown-up.

cards.q: An app crashed while you were playing. Is it your fault?
cards.note: Apps crash because of bugs in their instructions, not because of you. Just open it again.

cards.q: You are trying to fix a problem. How many fixes do you try at a time?
cards.note: Try one fix, then test. If you change ten things at once, you cannot tell which one helped.

cards.q: The tablet feels very warm. What does it need?
cards.note: A hot tablet needs a rest with the screen off, out of the sun and off the blanket. Never a bath.

cards.q: A grown-up asks what you were doing when it stopped. Why do they ask?
cards.note: What you were doing is a clue. It helps the grown-up find the bug, like a detective.
